output.impression: Neuropsychological evaluation demonstrates a predominantly amnestic profile with multi-domain involvement. Episodic memory is severely impaired: RAVLT immediate recall at the 4th percentile, delayed recall below the 1st percentile and recognition at the 3rd percentile, consistent with a storage-type deficit. Semantic fluency (Category Fluency, Animals, 6th percentile) and confrontation naming (Boston Naming Test, 20th percentile) are below expected norms. Executive function (Trail Making B, 12th percentile) is mildly reduced. Processing speed (Trail Making A, 34th percentile) and visuoconstructive ability (Rey Complex Figure Copy, 26th percentile) are within the normal range. Screening scores: MMSE 21/30, MoCA 16/30. Mood screening is borderline (GDS 5/15); cognitive deficits are disproportionate to any mood contribution. Multi-domain cognitive impairment with amnestic predominance, at a level consistent with mild dementia given the reported functional decline.

output.interpretation: Opening pressure 16 cmH2O. WBC 2 cells/uL (lymphocytes), RBC 0. Protein 41.2 mg/dL, glucose 72.5 mg/dL (CSF:serum ratio 0.61), all within reference ranges. Decreased Abeta42 (348 pg/mL) and Abeta42/40 ratio (0.044) with elevated p-tau181 (91 pg/mL) and total tau (547 pg/mL). This biomarker profile is consistent with Alzheimer disease pathology. Clinical correlation recommended.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: MMSE 21/30 with amnestic-predominant impairment not helped by category cues and informant-confirmed decline over two years; instrumental independence lost (finances, cooking, medicines and wayfinding), placing the syndrome at mild dementia
action_criteria.label: Perform a structured cognitive and behavioural assessment with informant history: a validated bedside instrument with the per-domain breakdown, whether delayed recall improves with cueing, and an explicit account of which instrumental activities have been lost. The syndrome must be documented before it is attributed
action_criteria.rationale: Whether this is mild cognitive impairment or dementia is decided clinically, by a validated instrument and the family's account of instrumental function, before any biomarker is interpreted [NIA_AA_2011].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Amnestic profile with disproportionate impairment of delayed recall and limited benefit from cueing, plus involvement of at least one other cognitive domain
action_criteria.label: Order comprehensive neuropsychological testing to characterize the cognitive profile and establish a baseline for tracking
action_criteria.rationale: Formal testing defines the domains involved beyond the bedside screen, weighs her low mood and tearfulness against the memory deficit, and sets a baseline for follow-up [NIA_AA_2011].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Normal TSH, B12 312 pg/mL with normal homocysteine and folate, non-reactive RPR and negative HIV: no reversible contributor; glucose 118 mg/dL and HbA1c 6.8% on metformin
action_criteria.label: Order the cognitive laboratory panel to identify reversible or contributing causes
action_criteria.rationale: Thyroid dysfunction, B12 deficiency (she takes metformin), syphilis, HIV and metabolic derangement are treatable contributors that must be excluded before the decline is attributed to a neurodegenerative cause [AAN_dementia_2018].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Bilateral hippocampal atrophy (Scheltens MTA grade 3) with temporoparietal-predominant cortical volume loss and frontal sparing; Fazekas grade 1 without infarct; normal brainstem and cerebellum
action_criteria.label: Obtain brain MRI with dementia (volumetric) protocol to assess medial-temporal atrophy and exclude vascular disease, hippocampal sclerosis, NPH, and mass lesions
action_criteria.rationale: Structural MRI excludes vascular, mass and hydrocephalic causes of the decline and shows whether the atrophy pattern supports Alzheimer disease [NIA_AA_2011].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Amyloid positivity: decreased CSF Abeta42/40 ratio with raised p-tau181 and total tau, or a positive amyloid PET
action_criteria.label: Establish amyloid status with CSF biomarkers or amyloid PET when the result would change management
action_criteria.rationale: Either CSF Abeta42/40 with p-tau or amyloid PET establishes amyloid status; one conclusive test is enough, and it is needed when the diagnosis remains uncertain after the clinical, neuropsychological and MRI assessment or when disease-modifying treatment is being considered [NIA_AA_2018] [Appropriate_Use_Amyloid_PET].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No interaction needing a dose change; counselling on additive gastrointestinal effects with metformin and alendronate, weight, and vagotonic bradycardia
action_criteria.label: Check donepezil against her current medicines before starting it
action_criteria.rationale: A cholinesterase inhibitor is offered for mild Alzheimer dementia; metformin and alendronate add gastrointestinal effects and amlodipine is reviewed for heart rate, although none is a contraindication [NICE_NG97].

prohibited_recommendations: Do not treat her low mood with a tricyclic antidepressant or paroxetine; their anticholinergic effect worsens cognition [Beers_2023].
Do not prescribe a benzodiazepine for her distress or tearfulness; benzodiazepines worsen cognition and raise fall and fracture risk in an older woman with osteoporosis [Beers_2023].
Do not attribute the decline to depression; borderline mood scores do not explain a storage-type amnestic deficit with loss of instrumental function.
Do not start memantine at the mild dementia stage; it is for moderate or severe Alzheimer disease or when cholinesterase inhibitors are not tolerated [NICE_NG97].
required_recommendations: Disclose the diagnosis of mild Alzheimer dementia to her, her husband and daughter, and discuss prognosis, advance care planning, durable power of attorney and carer support [NICE_NG97].

Address safety: supervised medicines (blister pack or a family member giving them, since a pill organizer alone has not prevented missed doses), continued supervision of cooking, finances kept with her husband, and a phone or identification for walks after she got lost.

Offer a trial of a cholinesterase inhibitor (donepezil, rivastigmine or galantamine) for mild Alzheimer dementia after checking pulse, conduction history and current medicines, with attention to gastrointestinal effects alongside metformin and alendronate [NICE_NG97].

Offer amyloid biomarker testing (CSF or amyloid PET) if a biological diagnosis would change management, such as eligibility for anti-amyloid treatment or diagnostic uncertainty; one conclusive test is sufficient [Appropriate_Use_Amyloid_PET].
Assess the depressive symptoms (GDS 5/15, tearfulness, loss of interest) and offer support; if an antidepressant is needed, prefer one with low anticholinergic burden such as sertraline.
Continue vascular risk management (blood pressure, diabetes with HbA1c 6.8% on metformin, statin) and encourage accompanied daily walking.

avoided_actions.rationale: ECG is unrelated to the dementia workup; no cardiac symptom or syncope to justify it in this case
Echocardiography is unrelated to the dementia workup; no cardioembolic indication in this presentation
Cardiac monitoring is not indicated; no arrhythmia, syncope, or palpitations described
Head CT adds little when MRI is available; MRI is the preferred structural modality for dementia workup

differential.key_features: No visual hallucinations, fluctuations, dream enactment or parkinsonism; the orthostatic dizziness three years ago resolved with amlodipine dose reduction and there is no orthostatic drop now; amnestic profile with temporoparietal atrophy

Loss of interest is accompanied by distress and insight, with no disinhibition, personality change, compulsions or hyperorality; no primary aphasia; amnestic profile with frontal sparing on MRI, and Alzheimer biomarkers when obtained
Diabetes, hypertension and a paternal stroke give vascular risk, but MRI shows only Fazekas grade 1 change without infarct and the course is gradual rather than stepwise

GDS 5/15, tearfulness and loss of interest suggest coexisting depressive symptoms, but recognition memory is impaired and cues do not help, which is not the pattern of depression-related cognitive impairment; mood is treated alongside, not instead of, the dementia diagnosis

differential.diagnosis: Reversible metabolic, endocrine, or sleep-related cognitive impairment
differential.key_features: TSH, B12 (312 pg/mL with normal homocysteine), folate, RPR and HIV are normal; no daytime somnolence; the progressive amnestic decline is not explained by any of these

key_clinical_evidence: Probable Alzheimer disease dementia is a clinical diagnosis under NIA-AA 2011: insidious onset, informant-confirmed progression, an amnestic presentation with another domain affected, and decline in usual activities; hippocampal and temporoparietal atrophy on MRI support it but are not required [NIA_AA_2011]
The hallmark cognitive feature of AD is impaired delayed recall with rapid forgetting and limited benefit from cueing, reflecting a storage-type (hippocampal) memory deficit
Depressive symptoms are common in early Alzheimer dementia; impaired recognition and no benefit from cues separate the neurodegenerative memory deficit from depression-related impairment
Cholinesterase inhibitors are indicated for mild to moderate Alzheimer dementia; memantine is for moderate or severe disease or when cholinesterase inhibitors are not tolerated [NICE_NG97]

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: It resolved after the amlodipine dose was reduced, has not recurred, and there is no orthostatic drop on examination; no parkinsonism, ataxia, hallucinations or dream enactment
red_herrings.intended_effect: Invites an autonomic work-up for a synucleinopathy (dementia with Lewy bodies or multiple system atrophy)

sequence_constraints.reason: Obtain structural imaging before lumbar puncture to exclude mass effect / herniation risk, particularly in older patients
Amyloid biomarkers are interpreted against an established clinical syndrome; they are not a screening test.

metadata.adaptation_notes: Clinical foundation inspired by published MSA case. Patient demographics modified to fit typical AD presentation (age increased to 73, cerebellar/autonomic features replaced with progressive amnestic syndrome). The source case's orthostatic dizziness is preserved as a historical finding attributed to medication, and the normal posterior fossa structures on MRI explicitly exclude MSA.

patient.history_present_illness: Mrs. Yumi Tanaka is a 73-year-old right-handed retired seamstress who presents to the outpatient neurology clinic accompanied by her daughter, Akiko, for evaluation of worsening memory difficulties over the past two years. The daughter first noticed subtle changes approximately two years ago when her mother began repeating questions during their weekly phone calls, sometimes asking the same question three or four times within a single conversation without apparent awareness of having done so. Over the following months, additional concerns emerged. Mrs. Tanaka, who had been an accomplished seamstress for decades, began making errors in sewing patterns she had known by heart for years, producing garments with misaligned seams and incorrect measurements. She also started having difficulty managing her household finances, a task she had handled independently for the entirety of her marriage. Her husband discovered several unpaid utility bills and noticed that the checkbook register contained arithmetic errors, which was highly unusual for her. Approximately one year ago, Mrs. Tanaka got lost walking home from the local market, a route she had taken daily for over twenty years, and had to call her daughter for directions. Since then, she has been reluctant to walk alone and prefers to stay in the apartment. She has forgotten to take her medications on multiple occasions, prompting her daughter to set up a pill organizer. Her cooking has also been affected; she has burned meals several times after forgetting she had left the stove on, and her husband now supervises all cooking activities. The daughter notes that her mother seems less interested in activities she previously enjoyed, including watching her favorite television programs and tending to her small balcony garden. Mrs. Tanaka acknowledges that her memory is not as good as it used to be and appears distressed about the changes, occasionally becoming tearful when discussing them. There have been no episodes of visual hallucinations, personality changes, or aggressive behavior. She has not experienced any falls, tremor, difficulty walking, seizures, or sudden onset neurological symptoms. Her sleep has been unremarkable according to her husband, with no reports of acting out dreams or excessive daytime somnolence. Three years ago, she experienced episodic dizziness upon standing that was evaluated and attributed to her antihypertensive medication; the amlodipine dose was reduced from 10 mg to 5 mg with resolution of symptoms. This prior orthostatic complaint has not recurred.

neurological_exam.additional: No paratonic rigidity. No grasp reflex. No myoclonus. No signs of parkinsonism. Orthostatic vital signs: supine BP 134/76, standing BP 128/72 at 3 minutes, no significant orthostatic drop.
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-to-nose testing intact bilaterally without dysmetria. Heel-to-shin testing normal. Rapid alternating movements intact. No past-pointing.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal, round, and reactive to light. Extraocular movements full without nystagmus. Visual fields full to confrontation. Facial sensation intact. Face symmetric with normal strength. Hearing grossly intact bilaterally. Palate elevates symmetrically. Sternocleidomastoid and trapezius strength 5/5 bilaterally. Tongue midline without fasciculations or atrophy.
neurological_exam.gait: Steady gait with normal base and stride length. Tandem gait intact. Romberg sign negative. No ataxia. Turns normally without instability.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented to person and place; knows the year and the season but cannot state the month, the exact date or the day of the week. MMSE 21/30, losing points on recall (0/3 at 5 minutes), orientation (3 points lost), attention/calculation (2 errors on serial sevens) and the three-stage command (1 point). Clock drawing test shows numbers clustered on the right side of the clock face with hands placed at an incorrect time. Unable to recall any of 3 words after 5 minutes, even with categorical cues. Naming intact for common objects but hesitates for less frequent items. Repetition intact. Comprehension intact for simple instructions but has difficulty following a three-step command. Fluency mildly reduced for category naming.
neurological_exam.motor: Bulk and tone normal throughout all extremities. No rigidity, no bradykinesia, no resting or postural tremor. Strength 5/5 in all extremities. No pronator drift.
neurological_exam.reflexes: 2+ and symmetric at biceps, triceps, brachioradialis, patellar, and Achilles bilaterally. Plantar responses flexor bilaterally. No Hoffmann sign. No Babinski sign.
neurological_exam.sensory: Intact to light touch, pinprick, vibration, and proprioception in all extremities. Mildly decreased vibration sense at bilateral great toes, attributed to age.
